network.pairing.refusal.answered.note: Deliberately says nothing about the outcome: an earlier answer may already have approved the device, or declined it.
network.pairing.refusal.answered.role: Desktop Mesh approvals: a second answer to a pairing that already has one (a double click, or another surface answered first)

network.pairing.refusal.expired.role: Desktop Mesh approvals: the pairing window closed or the card is out of date

network.pairing.refusal.mismatch.note: {count} is the number of tries left before the invitation is used up (0-3). Preserve the ICU plural arms, the =0 arm and # substitution; use the locale's CLDR plural forms.
network.pairing.refusal.mismatch.role: Desktop Mesh approvals: the typed six-digit code was wrong

network.pairing.refusal.needs_app.note: Shown when the answer could not be verified as coming from the signed desktop app (e.g. on Linux, or from a script). 'a terminal' refers to the command-line fallback; keep it generic, do not name commands.
network.pairing.refusal.needs_app.role: Desktop Mesh approvals: refusal when a pairing card is answered without the signed app

network.pairing.refusal.no_pending.note: 'invitation' is the pairing invite token minted on the other device.
network.pairing.refusal.no_pending.role: Desktop Mesh approvals: no pairing is waiting

network.pairing.refusal.not_ready.note: Pairing has two devices: the other device must first type the code this device shows.
network.pairing.refusal.not_ready.role: Desktop Mesh approvals: refusal while the other device has not typed the code
